speaker_concepts.verbatim_description: What actually moves the markets is the balance or imbalance between aggressive orders and passive orders.
These are the footprints that they leave behind [institutional activity], and institutions often defend these areas or finish filling uncompleted orders when price gets back to these areas.
Institutions cannot place an order this big and hide it. Their size leaves footprints.

speaker_concepts.term: Area of consolidation or a base
speaker_concepts.verbatim_description: This is what you want to look for on the chart: an area of consolidation or a base.
This is a strong and balanced candle moving away from that base.
This is where aggressive sellers stepped in and overwhelmed buyers, driving price down.
This is where aggressive buyers stepped in and overwhelmed sellers, pushing price higher.
My process is a top-down analysis, meaning I usually start on the 4 hour and refine my levels all the way down to the 30 minute.
I'm actually going to be looking for the candle immediately before the imbalance move. This is usually going to be a small basing candle of the opposite color.
This is usually going to be a small basing candle of the opposite color [followed by] a strong green imbalance candle.
You can actually refine your entries even more by using tools like bookmap so that you can see exactly where buyers and sellers are sitting at.
